[[File:Milan-Juventus 2018-2019 in game.jpg|thumb|Milan-Juventus 2018–2019 in game]]
The '''2018–19 [[Serie A]]''' (known as the '''Serie A [[Telecom Italia|TIM]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 117th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 87th in a [[round-robin tournament]], and the 9th since its organization under a league committee separate from [[Serie B]]. [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] were the seven-time defending champions and defended their title following their victory against [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] on 20 April 2019. The season was run from 18 August 2018 to 26 May 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forzaitalianfootball.com/2018/03/serie-a-and-coppa-italia-changes-for-2018-19-confirmed/|title=Serie A and Coppa Italia changes for 2018/19 confirmed - Forza Italian Football|website=forzaitalianfootball.com|date=5 March 2018}}</ref>

==Events==
[[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]] and [[Benevento Calcio|Benevento]] immediately returned to [[2018–19 Serie B|Serie B]] after finishing 19th and 20th while [[F.C. Crotone|Crotone]], finishing in 18th place, were relegated after two seasons in the top flight.

On 28 April, [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]] earned the right to come back to Serie A after one year of relegation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calciomercom/news/l-empoli-torna-in-a-caputo-co-una-macchina-da-gol-migliore-della-32674|title=L'Empoli torna in A: Caputo & co, una macchina da gol migliore della Juve|website=Calciomercato.com|access-date=16 July 2018}} {{Dead link|date=June 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On 18 May 2018, [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] achieved promotion having finished second in the [[2017–18 Serie B|2017–18 Serie B season]], just three seasons after their bankruptcy relegation to [[Serie D]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/121566/parma-return-serie|title=Parma return to Serie A!|publisher=Football Italia|date=18 May 2018}}</ref> The last team promoted, after 2 years of absence, was [[Frosinone Calcio|Frosinone]], who defeated [[U.S. Città di Palermo|Palermo]] in the Serie B play-off finals 3–2 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/123077/frosinone-promoted-serie|title=Frosinone promoted to Serie A! {{!}} Football Italia|website=Football-italia.net|access-date=2018-06-17}}</ref>

On 23 July, [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] were handed a 5-point deduction for the 2018–19 Serie A season, following text messages from Parma player [[Emanuele Calaiò]] "eliciting a reduced effort" from two players of [[Spezia Calcio|Spezia]] during the 2017–18 season, a match [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] won 2–0 to secure promotion to this season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/124854/parma-handed-five-point-deduction|title=Parma handed five-point deduction|publisher=Football Italia|date=23 July 2018}}</ref> On 9 August, [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] had the 5-point deduction expunged.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/soccer/story/parma-has-5-point-penalty-removed-calaio-ban-reduced-080918|title=Parma has 5-point penalty removed, Calaio ban reduced|work=foxsports.com|date=9 August 2018}}</ref>

On 14 August, the day of the [[Ponte Morandi]] bridge collapse in Genoa, the [[Italian Football Federation]] announced a minute's silence would be added for the victims of the collapse before all Serie A matches during the opening weekend that succeeded the incident.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/126164/minutes-silence-genoa-victims|title=Minute's silence for Genoa victims|publisher=Football Italia|date=14 August 2018}}</ref> On 16 August, the [[Lega Serie A]] postponed the opening matches for both Genoese clubs [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]] and [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] that were originally scheduled for 19 August.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/126278/official-sampdoria-genoa-matches|title=Official: Sampdoria, Genoa matches off|publisher=Football Italia|date=16 August 2018}}</ref>

On 13 September, Chievo was deducted 3 points after being found guilty of false accounting.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/127901/chievo-get-three-point-deduction|title=Chievo get three point deduction|publisher=Football Italia|date=13 September 2018}}</ref>

On 14 April 2019, Chievo was relegated from Serie A after a 3–1 defeat by Napoli, ending an eleven-year spell in the top flight.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/136989/koulibaly-brace-relegates-chievo|title=Koulibaly brace relegates Chievo {{!}} Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net|date=14 April 2019|access-date=2019-04-24}}</ref>

On 20 April, Juventus won their 35th title and their eighth in a row with a win over Fiorentina.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/137199/juventus-fightback-secure-scudetto|title=Juventus fightback to secure Scudetto {{!}} Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net|access-date=2019-04-22}}</ref>

On 5 May, Frosinone was relegated from Serie A after a 2–2 draw away at Sassuolo, going down after just one season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ronaldo.com/football-news/frosinone-was-relegated-to-the-serie-b/|title=Frosinone was relegated to the Serie B - ronaldo.com|first=Manuel R.|last=Medina|date=5 May 2019|website=ronaldo.com|accessdate=6 March 2023|archive-date=25 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220425040316/https://ronaldo.com/football-news/frosinone-was-relegated-to-the-serie-b/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 26 May, [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]] finished third and secured a place in the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stage, both for the first time in their history.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-italy-att-sas-report/atalanta-reach-champions-league-for-the-first-time-idUKKCN1SW0W9|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526212136/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-italy-att-sas-report/atalanta-reach-champions-league-for-the-first-time-idUKKCN1SW0W9|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 May 2019|title=Atalanta reach Champions League for the first time|work=Reuters|date=26 May 2019}}</ref> Meanwhile, Empoli which were one point above the relegation zone ahead of Genoa, were eventually relegated to Serie B after they were defeated by [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]], while Genoa drew with [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].

This was also the last season of iconic [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] captain [[Daniele De Rossi]] that left the team after 18 seasons,<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.football-italia.net/138032/official-de-rossi-leave-roma| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190514132543/https://www.football-italia.net/138032/official-de-rossi-leave-roma| archive-date = 2019-05-14| title = OFFICIAL: De Rossi to leave Roma {{!}} Football Italia}}</ref> while veterans [[Sergio Pellissier]] (from [[A.C. ChievoVerona|Chievo]]),<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.football-italia.net/137883/chievos-pellissier-retire| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190510211054/https://www.football-italia.net/137883/chievos-pellissier-retire| archive-date = 2019-05-10| title = Chievo's Pellissier to retire {{!}} Football Italia}}</ref> [[Andrea Barzagli]] (from [[Juventus FC|Juventus]])<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/136947/barzagli-announces-retirement|title = Barzagli announces retirement|date = 13 April 2019}}</ref> and [[Emiliano Moretti]] (from [[Torino F.C.|Torino]])<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Torino/22-05-2019/moretti-annuncia-ritiro-si-commuove-grazie-toro-ma-momento-giusto-3301833021922.shtml|title=Moretti annuncia il ritiro e si commuove: "Grazie Toro, ma è il momento giusto"|date=2019|access-date=26 May 2019|archive-date=21 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121212930/https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Torino/22-05-2019/moretti-annuncia-ritiro-si-commuove-grazie-toro-ma-momento-giusto-3301833021922.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> retired from professional football at the end of the season.
